patient.chief_complaint: Wife called 911 - husband having continuous left-sided focal seizure spreading to bilateral convulsions, 15 minutes
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Clarke is a 52-year-old man with left temporal focal epilepsy on carbamazepine who is brought by ambulance after his wife called 911 when he developed a focal seizure with left-sided onset involving right hand automatisms and lip smacking, which secondarily generalized after 2 minutes. The seizure has been continuous for 15 minutes. He took his medications yesterday but his wife is not sure about his compliance over the past week as he has been working very long hours with minimal sleep. He started a new 10-day antibiotic course 4 days ago for community-acquired pneumonia — he was prescribed clarithromycin by his primary care physician. This is a critical drug interaction: clarithromycin is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor and carbamazepine is metabolized by CYP3A4. Additionally, carbamazepine induces its own metabolism (autoinduction). However, with a CYP3A4 inhibitor like clarithromycin, carbamazepine levels actually INCREASE rather than decrease — because clarithromycin blocks carbamazepine metabolism, leading to carbamazepine toxicity. Paradoxically, the SE may be partially from carbamazepine toxicity (pro-convulsant at very high levels) rather than subtherapeutic levels. The valproate allergy (thrombocytopenia and pancreatitis) significantly limits second-line AED choices. His hypothyroidism is stable on levothyroxine.
